data.title: Airbus sees Asia-Pacific jet demand holding firm despite global headwinds
data.description:
Airbus (EADSF)(EADSY) continues to see robust demand for commercial aircraft, with airlines showing little sign that geopolitical tensions or supply-chain disruptions are weakening their appetite for new jets.

Anand Stanley, president of Airbus Asia-Pacific, said during a market outlook briefing in Hong Kong that customers remain eager to accept aircraft, Reuters reported Tuesday. Delivery activity also is strengthening in Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and other regions.

The European aircraft manufacturer has delivered 9% more planes so far this year than during the comparable period of 2025, according to Stanley.

For Airbus (EADSF)(EADSY) investors, steady demand and rising deliveries support the outlook for revenue, cash flow and production growth. The company already has a substantial order backlog, so its near-term financial performance depends less on finding buyers than on securing engines, components and labor to build aircraft on schedule. Asia-Pacific’s projected share of worldwide deliveries also gives Airbus significant exposure to one of aviation’s strongest long-term growth markets. The main investor risk remains execution: demand can be abundant while supply constraints delay deliveries and the payments tied to them.

Asia-Pacific to claim nearly half of new aircraft

Airbus (EADSF)(EADSY) estimates that airlines worldwide will require approximately 42,000 new aircraft during the next two decades. About 45% of those planes are expected to go to Asia-Pacific customers as passenger traffic expands and carriers replace older fleets.

China alone is projected to need 8,830 new passenger aircraft during the period, making it Airbus’ largest individual commercial aviation market. India is expected to require 3,480 aircraft, while the remainder of Asia-Pacific will account for another 6,880.

François Cabaret, who leads Airbus’ global market forecasting, said Chinese airlines have fallen behind their previous fleet-renewal pace. Before the pandemic, carriers in China accepted about 400 aircraft annually. Combined deliveries from Airbus, Boeing and COMAC have since dropped to fewer than half that level.

That gap creates potential for a sizable replacement cycle, although the timing will depend on China’s economic growth, airline finances and the ability of manufacturers to increase production.

India accelerates as China forecast cools

Airbus (EADSF)(EADSY) expects passenger traffic across Asia to grow by an average of 5.1% a year over the next two decades, but that expansion will not be evenly distributed.

India remains the fastest-growing major aviation market. Airbus increased its forecast for annual domestic traffic growth in the country to 9.3% from 8.9%.

The company lowered its comparable projection for China to 4.7% from 5.4%. Cabaret attributed the reduction to the country’s broader economic conditions rather than an excessive supply of aircraft or airline capacity.

Smaller cities create new routes

Airbus (EADSF)(EADSY) also expects urban growth to create demand beyond Asia’s largest metropolitan areas. Approximately 600 new small and midsize cities could emerge around the world over the next 20 years, supporting additional airports and routes.

The company sees its A220 and A321XLR as well suited to that shift. Airlines have used the smaller A220 to establish more than 400 routes worldwide, and Airbus believes the aircraft could make another 800 city pairs viable in Asia-Pacific.

The longer-range A321XLR could create more than 2,200 additional route opportunities in the region. Its ability to fly distances traditionally served by wide-body aircraft gives airlines a way to test thinner international routes without committing to a much larger plane.

data.title: ScottsMiracle-Gro redeems $250M in notes, begins share buyback
data.description:
ScottsMiracle-Gro (SMG) said Tuesday it redeemed $250 million of senior notes, renewed a major financing facility and began buying back shares as the lawn and garden products company works to reduce debt while returning capital to stockholders.

The company redeemed all of its 5.25% senior notes due in 2026 on Sept. 11. It funded the repayment with borrowings under its revolving credit facility and excess free cash flow expected during fiscal 2026.

ScottsMiracle-Gro (SMG) also renewed a $750 million accounts receivable facility with J.P. Morgan Chase, extending its maturity through Aug. 31, 2027. Such facilities let companies obtain liquidity using customer receivables and can help support working-capital needs.

For investors, the debt repayment removes a near-term maturity but does not eliminate the obligation because ScottsMiracle-Gro (SMG) partly replaced the notes with revolver borrowings. The company’s projected $275 million in free cash flow could help reduce that balance. Meanwhile, the buyback may support per-share results, though management said debt reduction will take priority over additional repurchases.

ScottsMiracle-Gro (SMG) spent $25 million repurchasing shares in August, beginning a previously authorized $500 million program. The company said the pace and size of future purchases will depend on market conditions, leverage goals and other financial priorities.

The company reaffirmed its fiscal 2026 forecast, including low-single-digit sales growth in its U.S. Consumer business, adjusted gross margin of at least 32% and adjusted earnings of $4.30 to $4.45 a share. It continues to expect mid-single-digit adjusted EBITDA growth, $275 million in free cash flow and a year-end leverage ratio in the high-three-times range.

ScottsMiracle-Gro’s (SMG) fiscal year ends Sept. 30. The company plans to report its full-year results on Nov. 4.

data.title: Brookfield, Canada Pension Plan launch C$50B Maple Fund
data.description:
Brookfield Asset Management (BAM) and the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board agreed to create a fund   with the aim to invest up to C$50B (US$36B) in large-scale investments in critical infrastructure and strategic industries across Canada, they said on Tuesday.

The announcement came a day after TD Bank (TD) launched a five-year C$150B commitment to accelerate investment, growth, and innovation across critical industries in Canada and follows blueprints similar to  JPMorgan Chase's (JPM) US$1.5T Security and Resilience Initiative announced almost a year ago.

CPP Investments and Brookfield (BAM) will structure investments on a 50/50 basis with up to C$25B of Maple Fund equity capital from each entity over an initial five-year period. The partnership will seek opportunities with total project values exceeding C$5B in equity capital. Other investors may partner with the two organizations on individual investments, further expanding the capital and capabilities available, CPP and Brookfield said.

"CPP Investments has the capital, long-term investment horizon, and expertise to pursue these opportunities, and the Maple Fund brings together our strengths with Brookfield's strong origination and development capabilities to help move ambitious projects from opportunity to investment," said CPP Investments President and CEO John Graham. "The Maple Fund positions us well to meet this moment and move with speed on opportunities of unusual scale and complexity when they offer compelling value for the CPP Fund."

Brookfield Asset Management (BAM) stock crept up 0.2% in Tuesday premarket trading.

data.title: Sempra signs 20-year U.S. LNG supply deal with Petrobras
data.description:
Sempra (SRE) said late Monday it signed a 20-year sales and purchase agreement with Petrobras (PBR), in which Sempra Infrastructure will supply 800K metric tons/year of liquefied natural gas sourced from liquefaction capacity at the Port Arthur LNG Phase 2 project, currently under construction in Texas.

Petrobras (PBR) represents the first South American company in Sempra Infrastructure's (SRE) LNG customer portfolio, CEO Justin Bird said.

Port Arthur Phase 2 reached a final investment decision in September 2025 and is designed to add 13M metric tons/year of liquefaction capacity through two additional trains; the 13M tons/year Phase 1 is already under construction, with its two trains targeted to start commercial operations in 2027 and 2028.

Sempra (SRE),which has estimated project capital spending at $12B plus $2B for shared facilities with Phase 1, has lined up several major customers for Phase 2 ahead of its investment decision.

data.title: Bally's lands key financing for its Bronx casino resort project
data.description:
Bally's Corporation (BALY) updated investors this week that its $560M financing package will help its planned $4B Bronx casino resort move forward. The funds will go toward pre-construction planning and help Bally's (BALY) stay on schedule while it completes the broader capital raise. The loan is expected to close during the current quarter, subject to approvals and customary conditions.

In its application materials in New York, Bally's (BALY) set a construction timeline of eight to nine months after securing a license and a single-phase opening sometime in 2030.

The project, known as Bally’s Bronx, is planned for a 16-acre portion of Bally’s Golf Links at Ferry Point near the Whitestone Bridge—land formerly associated with Trump Golf Links. Bally's (BALY) bought the key city-owned parcel for about $156.6M earlier this year, giving it control of the clubhouse, parking, and access areas needed for the development.

Plans call for a roughly 3M-square-foot, 19-story waterfront complex. Key elements include a casino with approximately 3,500 slot machines, about 210 table games and poker; a 500-room hotel; more than 10 food-and-beverage venues; a 2,000-person event or convention center; and about 4,600 parking spaces. Bally's (BALY) has also proposed retaining golf- and park-related amenities around the resort and investing more than $160M in nearby Ferry Point Park and Throggs Neck improvements.

data.title: Lilly to invest in QurCan as part of genetic medicines deal
data.description:
Canadian biotech QurCan Therapeutics on Tuesday announced an investment from Eli Lilly (LLY) as part of an exclusive research and collaboration agreement with the Indiana-based pharma giant to develop genetic medicines.

The deal focuses on leveraging QurCan’s TERP (Target-Engineered Responsive Polymer) platform to develop genetic medicines that target the central and peripheral nervous systems.

Under the agreement, QurCan will lead the initial research, after which Eli Lilly (LLY) will take over further research, clinical development, and commercialization.

The Toronto-based firm will receive an upfront payment and a strategic investment from Lilly (LLY) as part of the deal. Additionally, the company will be entitled to a per-program payment of up to $237M, which represents R&D support payments as well as research, development, and commercial milestone payments.

QurCan will also receive tiered royalties as a percentage of global net sales of commercialized products.

The multi-program collaboration marks Eli Lilly’s (LLY) latest as the weight-loss drugmaker looks to step up its deal-making activity driven by record-breaking sales from its obesity franchise. In late August, the company agreed to buy privately held Merida Biosciences for up to $2.9B in cash to boost its immunology portfolio.
